messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Mendelian randomization found no evidence that genetically proxied 25-OH-D levels causally affect major depressive disorder.
Sentence: "In summary-level data analyses, 2SMR analyses provided no evidence of a causal role on MDD of 25-OH-D (p = 0.50) or n3-PUFA (p = 0.16), or for a causal role of MDD on 25-OH-D (p = 0.25) or n3-PUFA (p = 0.66)."
Measured as: major depressive disorder (MDD)
Population: GWAS summary data: 25-OH-D (N = 79,366) and MDD (135,458 cases, 344,901 controls)
Intervention: Genetically proxied circulating 25-OH-D levels (two-sample Mendelian randomization)
Comparator: Lower genetically proxied 25-OH-D levels
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 480,359
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Patients with depression had lower estimated daily vitamin D doses from all sources than healthy controls.
Sentence: "Patients with depression had a lower dose of vitamin D (IU) per day with 234, 153, and 81 per day from all sources, sunlight exposure, and dietary intake, respectively."
Measured as: depression (case vs control status) by estimated daily vitamin D dose
Population: 96 patients with depression age- and sex-matched with 96 healthy controls
Intervention: Estimated cumulative vitamin D dose from solar ultraviolet exposure and dietary intake (observational)
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 192
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
